hero.subtitle: AAPI adults develop type 2 diabetes at BMI 23 — not 25. Our culturally-tailored screening tool, community resources, and health data empower you to take control.

pillars.title: Three Pillars of Health Equity
pillars.subtitle: Combining data, culturally-competent screening, and community resources to address disparities.
pillars.screening_desc: Using the ADA-recommended BMI ≥23 threshold for AAPI populations instead of the standard ≥25 cutoff. Our risk calculator considers ethnicity sub-groups, waist circumference, and family history patterns specific to AAPI communities.
pillars.data_desc: Real-time data from the NYC Community Health Survey and Open Data API, visualized on an interactive map to identify high-risk neighborhoods and track diabetes prevalence across all five boroughs.
pillars.resources_desc: A directory of 150+ AAPI-serving nonprofits funded by the $54.35M Equity Budget, with support in 20+ languages. Plus a hospital language compliance tracker to ensure your rights under the new Hospital Language Access Law.

landing.cta_text: The ADA recommends diabetes screening for AAPI adults starting at BMI 23. Don't wait until 25 — early detection can prevent or delay type 2 diabetes.

compliance.title: Hospital Language Compliance
compliance.subtitle: Tracking compliance with the Hospital Language Access Law (S6288B/A387B) signed December 2025.
compliance.info_title: Your Rights Under the New Law
compliance.info_text: All general hospitals in New York must provide: a Language Assistance Coordinator, timely patient identification for language needs, translated materials for any language group ≥1% of the service area, and ongoing staff training on culturally competent care.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: AAPI Health Equity ("we", "us", "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This policy explains how we handle your information when you use our platform.
privacy.section_collection_text: Our diabetes risk screener processes health data (age, height, weight, waist circumference, family history, ethnicity) entirely in your browser. This data is never sent to any server. We do not collect personally identifiable information unless you voluntarily provide it through our subscription forms.
privacy.section_storage_text: We use your browser's local storage to save your language preference and notification settings. This data stays on your device and is not transmitted to us.
privacy.section_analytics_text: We do not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics services. Your browsing activity on this platform is not monitored or recorded.
privacy.section_health_text: All health screening data entered into our Risk Screener is processed client-side only. No health information is stored, transmitted, or shared with any third party. Your screening results are generated in real-time and are not retained after you close or navigate away from the page.
privacy.section_third_party_text: Our platform uses OpenStreetMap for map data and CARTO for map tiles. These services may collect anonymized usage data according to their own privacy policies. We also link to external resources (NYC Open Data, nonprofit organizations) whose privacy practices we do not control.
privacy.section_rights_text: You have the right to: clear your local storage data at any time through your browser settings, opt out of any communications, and request information about what data (if any) we hold. Since we process data client-side, there is typically no server-side data to delete.
privacy.section_contact_text: If you have questions about this privacy policy, please reach out to us through the AAPI Health Equity Project's open-source community channels.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By using the AAPI Health Equity platform, you agree to the following terms and conditions.
terms.section_medical_text: This platform provides health information and a diabetes risk screening tool for educational purposes only. The risk screener is not a medical diagnosis. Results should not be used as a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider for medical concerns.
terms.section_accuracy_text: We strive to provide accurate and up-to-date information based on ADA guidelines and NYC public health data. However, we make no warranties about the completeness, reliability, or accuracy of this information. Health guidelines may change, and data may not reflect the most current statistics.
terms.section_use_text: You agree to use this platform for lawful purposes only. You may not attempt to reverse-engineer, modify, or redistribute the platform's code without complying with its open-source license. You may not use the platform to collect personal data of other users.
terms.section_ip_text: The AAPI Health Equity platform is an open-source project. The source code is available under its respective license. Content, design elements, and branding remain the property of the AAPI Health Equity Project.
terms.section_liability_text: To the fullest extent permitted by law, the AAPI Health Equity Project shall not be liable for any damages arising from your use of this platform, including but not limited to health decisions made based on screening results.
terms.section_changes_text: We reserve the right to modify these terms at any time. Continued use of the platform constitutes acceptance of updated terms.

a11y.title: Accessibility Statement
a11y.intro: The AAPI Health Equity Project is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people of all abilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards.
a11y.section_standards_text: We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA. These guidelines define how to make web content more accessible to people with disabilities.
a11y.feature_keyboard: Full keyboard navigation throughout the application
a11y.feature_screen_reader: Screen reader compatibility with ARIA labels and roles
a11y.feature_contrast: High color contrast ratios for text readability
a11y.feature_language: Multilingual support in 5 languages including RTL (Urdu)
a11y.feature_responsive: Responsive design for mobile, tablet, and desktop
a11y.feature_focus: Visible focus indicators for interactive elements
a11y.section_limitations_text: While we strive for full accessibility, some limitations exist: the interactive map relies on visual markers that may not be fully accessible to screen reader users, and some emoji icons used for visual emphasis may not convey meaning through assistive technology.
a11y.section_feedback_text: We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of this platform. If you encounter accessibility barriers or have suggestions for improvement, please contact us through our open-source project channels. We take accessibility feedback seriously and aim to respond within 5 business days.

bill.banner_text: 🎉 The Screen at 23 Act (S634B) has passed the Senate & Assembly! Free diabetes screenings at BMI 23 are coming for NYC residents.
bill.modal_title: The Screen at 23 Act Just Passed!
bill.modal_text: New York's Bill S634B will require health insurers to cover diabetes screenings at BMI ≥23 for AAPI populations — with zero out-of-pocket costs. This is a historic win for health equity.
bill.page_subtitle: A historic bill requiring insurance coverage for diabetes screenings at the AAPI-appropriate BMI threshold of 23.
bill.timeline_introduced_desc: S634B introduced in the NY State Senate to address AAPI diabetes screening disparities.
bill.timeline_senate_desc: The Senate passed S634B as part of the affordable healthcare package for AAPI communities.
bill.timeline_assembly_desc: The Assembly companion bill passed, sending the legislation to the Governor's desk.
bill.timeline_governor_desc: The bill is now awaiting the Governor's signature to become law. Once signed, insurers must comply.
bill.benefit_screening_desc: Diabetes screening will be covered with no copay, coinsurance, or deductible when your BMI is 23 or above — the medically appropriate threshold for AAPI populations.
bill.benefit_insurance_desc: All New York health insurance policies will be required to cover these screenings, removing financial barriers to early detection.
bill.benefit_care_desc: Healthcare providers will follow evidence-based guidelines specifically developed for AAPI populations, recognizing the different risk profiles across ethnic sub-groups.
bill.benefit_outreach_desc: The bill supports targeted outreach to AAPI communities through multilingual education and awareness programs.
bill.prepare_step1_desc: Use our Risk Screener to calculate your BMI and understand your risk level using AAPI-specific thresholds.
bill.prepare_step2_desc: Bring up the Screen at 23 threshold with your healthcare provider and ask about scheduling a diabetes screening.
bill.prepare_step3_desc: Contact your health insurer to ask about their plans for compliance with S634B once it becomes law.
bill.prepare_step4_desc: Share this information with your family and community so more people can benefit from free screenings.
bill.faq_q1: When will the bill take effect?
bill.faq_a1: The bill is currently awaiting the Governor's signature. Once signed, insurers will have a compliance period (typically 90-180 days) to update their coverage policies.
bill.faq_q2: Who is eligible for free screenings?
bill.faq_a2: The bill covers diabetes and pre-diabetes screenings for individuals whose BMI is 23 or above, based on evidence-based guidelines for AAPI populations. It applies to anyone covered by a New York health insurance policy.
bill.faq_a3: The bill covers diabetes and pre-diabetes screening tests, including A1C tests and fasting glucose tests, without out-of-pocket costs such as copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles.
bill.faq_q4: Does this apply to all insurance plans?
bill.faq_a4: The bill applies to health insurance policies issued in New York State. Federal plans (such as Medicare) have their own coverage rules and may not be directly affected.
bill.faq_q5: What if my BMI is below 23?
bill.faq_a5: Standard screening guidelines still apply. If you have other risk factors (family history, ethnicity, age), your doctor may recommend screening regardless of BMI. Our Risk Screener can help you assess your overall risk.
bill.subscribe_text: Get notified when the Governor signs the bill and when free screenings become available.
bill.subscribe_success: You're subscribed! We'll notify you when S634B becomes law.

default_tasks.t1_title: Calculate Diabetes Risk Score at BMI ≥23
default_tasks.t1_desc: Use our AAPI Diabetes Risk Screener to evaluate your baseline risk using ADA cutoff guidelines.
default_tasks.t2_desc: Book an appointment with your primary care provider and request Fasting Blood Glucose and HbA1c tests.
default_tasks.t3_title: Request Language Assistance Coordinator under S6288B
default_tasks.t3_desc: When visiting hospital or clinic, exercise your legal right under Hospital Language Access Law to get free interpreter service.
default_tasks.t4_title: Connect with Local Funded AAPI Non-Profit (CBO)
default_tasks.t4_desc: Find an organization from our 150+ CBO directory (such as SACSS or MinKwon) for culturally tailored wellness support.
default_tasks.t5_title: Verify Insurance Coverage for BMI ≥23 Screening
default_tasks.t5_desc: Confirm zero out-of-pocket cost coverage for diabetes screening under S634B Screen at 23 Act guidelines.
default_tasks.t6_title: Track Waist Circumference and Physical Activity
default_tasks.t6_desc: Log weekly active minutes (aim for 150 mins/week) and monitor waist measurement (cutoffs: 90cm men, 80cm women).
default_tasks.t7_desc: Incorporate whole grain or brown rice alternatives, fiber-rich traditional vegetables, and reduce sugary drinks.
